Bring a quieter kind of statement into your home
Story-first landscape photography and heirloom metal prints shaped by real places, changing light, and the lived experience of the coast.

Some photographs are made to decorate a wall. Others change the feeling of a room. At Cascadia Oceanic, each piece begins with place as lived experience—moments returned to, noticed carefully, and shaped into artwork that invites a second look.

column4: >Modern 2025: two images that hold memory in very different ways. One reflects the quiet power of a long-abandoned boat near the Samish River in Washington. The other captures an enduring roadside landmark in Aquebogue, New York, where nostalgia and personal history meet the everyday landscape.

column1: For collectors, homeowners, and anyone who wants art with real presence, these ChromaLuxe metal prints offer more than a view. They bring story, craftsmanship, and a lasting connection to place into the spaces where life happens every day.

column2: >Wreck 2025 — Quiet depth with history. Shot on a dark late October morning near Edison, Washington, this image turns a forgotten wooden boat into a meditation on time, memory, and what remains.

>Modern 2025 — Everyday landmark, lasting meaning. Captured in Aquebogue, New York, this mid-century sign stands as a marker of personal history and place—proof that familiar scenes often carry the deepest stories.
>Crafted for modern spaces. Each image is printed on ChromaLuxe gloss white aluminum for a clean, contemporary presentation with rich detail, clarity, and durability.
>Made to live with, not just look at. These are pieces for homes and offices that value calm, authenticity, and a deeper connection to landscape over mass-produced wall décor.

column1: If one of these images speaks to your own memories of coastlines, roadside landmarks, weather, or return journeys, that response matters. Cascadia Oceanic was built around the idea that photography can do more than show a scene—it can hold a pace, a season, and a sense of belonging.

column6: padding-top:8px"">Come see my latest work at the Bellevue Arts Fair

column5: padding-top:10px"">July 24–26 • New work, metal prints, and the chance to experience these images at their intended scale.

column1: Some images are meant to be lived with, not just scrolled past. That’s one reason I’m especially excited to share my latest work in person at the <span style=""color:#174A2E

This will be a chance to see Cascadia Oceanic prints the way they’re intended to be seen: at full scale, with their full tonal range, and with enough time to let the story of each place unfold. My work has always been rooted in a quiet attention to landscape, weather, memory, and the changing character of the coast and beyond.

I’ll be bringing recent pieces from the Pacific Northwest along with a few newer works shaped by travel, early light, and those brief moments when a place seems to reveal itself all at once. If you’ll be at the fair, I’d love for you to stop by and spend a little time with the work.

column2: font-weight:bold"">Thoughtful presentation: Landscape photography rewards time, distance, and detail. Seeing the work in person changes the experience.
font-weight:bold"">Story-first images: Each piece is rooted in place, atmosphere, and lived experience rather than postcard spectacle.
font-weight:bold"">Metal print craftsmanship: These ChromaLuxe aluminum prints bring out depth, clarity, and a clean modern finish that suits contemporary spaces beautifully.
font-weight:bold"">New perspectives: I’ll be showing recent work including pieces like Wharf 2026, Deception 2026, and Snoqualmie 2026, along with other newer images.
font-weight:bold"">Real conversation: One of the best parts of a fair like this is the chance to talk directly about process, place, and how an image might live in your home.
